inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average ordinary shares for H1 FY2026 (3,378,674,991; interim report Note 26, line 3370). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Basic weighted average was 3,255.5m; the 123m gap is unvested RSUs/options. Buybacks (RMB3.08bn in H1 2026, ~US$2.99bn cumulative since Sept 2022) continue to shrink the count below this figure, so the divisor is slightly conservative. 1 BEKE ADS = 3 Class A ordinary shares.
inputs.net_cash_composition: RMB m at 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 interim balance sheet + Notes 5 and 13): cash and cash equivalents 7,387.0; short-term investments 39,585.9 (bank time deposits 10,998.7, wealth-management products 21,302.0, HTM debt 2,057.9, AFS debt 5,227.3); long-term treasury-like investments 17,452.8 (long-term time deposits 1,841.9 + HTM debt 10,703.2 + wealth-management products at fair value 4,907.7). Total treasury 64,425.7. Less borrowings: short-term 85.8 + long-term current portion 191.7 + related-party loan payables 1,081.6 current + 366.2 non-current = 1,725.3. EXCLUDED: restricted cash 9,039.1 (buyer escrow, matched by customer deposits payable 5,685 and rental deposits held for others); equity-method investees 1,910.7 and minor equity stakes 163 (not treasury, left out as a conservative simplification); operating lease liabilities 12,662.9 (see lease_treatment); financing receivables 2,551.8 (operating asset of the financial-services line). Company's own headline 'cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments' is RMB56.0bn; this build adds the long-term time deposits/HTM/WMPs and removes escrow. No onshore-cash haircut applied: the company has repatriated ~US$3bn for buybacks plus RMB2.9bn/yr dividends, and the 28% cash-tax rate above the 25% PRC statutory rate already carries repatriation withholding.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement add-back 'Share-based compensation expenses': FY2025 RMB1,904.9m (Annual FY2025 line 6990), H1 FY2026 905.1m and H1 FY2025 1,016.4m (interim line 1333). TTM = 1,904.9 + 905.1 - 1,016.4 = 1,793.6. No cash taxes on net-share settlement disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes KPI = 0), so the add-back is the full figure.
inputs.fcf_basis: TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY2025 + H1 FY2026 - H1 FY2025, in RMB m. Reported FCF (OCF - capex): FY2025 -983.9 (OCF -376.2, capex 607.7); H1 2026 4,896.0 (OCF 5,140.8, capex 244.8); H1 2025 -3,621.4 (OCF -3,139.1, capex 482.3); TTM 7,533.5. Treasury income stripped (interest_income field): net interest income TTM 576.5 (807.5 + 261.5 - 492.5) plus investment income on wealth-management products/time deposits booked in 'Other income, net' TTM 724.9 (721.6 + 340.7 - 337.4, Annual FY2025 Note 17 and interim Note 19) = 1,301.4. Owner FCF TTM = 7,533.5 - 1,793.6 - 1,301.4 = 4,438.5. FY2025 alone is NOT used as the base: owner FCF was -3,697 because RMB6.7bn of working capital unwound (accounts payable -3,344, employee compensation payable -1,910, inventories -1,251, lease liability/ROU net -515, prepayments -1,006), most of which reversed in H1 2026. The forward path is built from components, so the base-year FCF is a disclosure, not a driver.
inputs.buyback_note: Financing-activity outflow 'Repurchase of ordinary shares': FY2025 RMB6,581.2m, H1 2026 3,079.6m (TTM 6,830.4m). Dividends paid: FY2025 2,881.2m, H1 2026 2,066.6m. Total shareholder returns ~RMB9.5bn/yr exceed owner FCF (~4.4-5.5bn) and are funded from the treasury, which is consistent with adding the full net cash to EV and holding the count flat. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model; the flat count is being funded.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. All per-share values computed in CNY then converted at CNY/HKD 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16T22:01Z). Direction: model CNY -> quote HKD, multiply. Parity check against the NYSE primary listing: BEKE ADS closed US$18.07 on 2026-10-16 (NYSE, ~12h after the HK close); 1 ADS = 3 Class A shares -> US$6.023/share x ~7.77 USD/HKD = HK$46.8 vs the HK$47.46 HKEX close, a 1.4% tie that confirms the quote basis and the ADS ratio. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive fx_rate at the next rebuild.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z (HKEX regular close, Friday; valuation written Sunday 2026-10-18)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the flows' currency. 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8-2.0%; China equity risk premium ~6.5% (mature-market 4.5% + country premium); beta ~1.2 for a housing-transaction cyclical; +0.5pp for the VIE/weighted-voting-rights structure and offshore-holder governance. Cost of equity ~10%; the company is debt-free (RMB1.7bn borrowings against RMB64bn treasury) so WACC = cost of equity = 10.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and property-market risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (Carefree Rent apartment leases and store leases; operating lease liabilities RMB12,662.9m at 2026-06-30, down from 17,628.1m at FY2025 as the rental model shifts asset-light). Rent is expensed in cost of revenues and the cash flows through OCF, so the lease charge is already inside the EBITDA margin anchor (treatment B equivalent). Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt and no lease_cost_pct_path is used. The ROU-asset / lease-liability lines in OCF (FY2025 net -515m, H1 2026 net +915m) are accrual timing and net toward zero through the cycle.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests RMB59.5m on the balance sheet, RMB0.6m share of H1 2026 net income (RMB2.9m FY2025): immaterial. Flows modelled consolidated, no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Company 'Adjusted EBITDA' (net income + tax + SBC + D&A - net interest income - fair-value changes + impairments) LESS the investment income on wealth-management products and time deposits that the company books in 'Other income, net' (FY2024 679.3, FY2025 721.6, H1 2026 340.7, H1 2025 337.4). Government grants (FY2025 600.9m, H1 2026 320.7m; VAT super-deductions and local subsidies) are retained as recurring. Anchors (RMB m, % of revenue): FY2023 11,344.7 headline (~13.7% ex investment income); FY2024 9,533.7 - 679.3 = 8,854 (9.5%); FY2025 6,876.6 - 721.6 = 6,155 (6.5%, trough: new-home GTV -8%, renovation channel exit, FY2025 pre-restructuring cost base); H1 2026 ~6,400 - 341 = ~6,060 (~13.6-14.0%, gross margin +6.7pp YoY, opex -14%); TTM ~8,550 (9.6%). The margin is pre-SBC; SBC is charged separately via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 2: non-US, cyclical operating company), with the adaptations for reporting-vs-quote currency, leases, excluded treasury income and charge-risk-once. KE Holdings is an operating housing-transaction platform, not a financial, REIT or holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF or memory entry). FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end), so year 1 of the path is FY2026 (H1 already reported: revenue -12.0%, GTV +6.3% in Q2). Base-year revenue is FY2025 actual; FCF anchors are TTM to June 2026 (see fcf_basis). Price is the Friday HKEX regular close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle base-case growth (years 2-5 average), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-1.2% 3yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+16% 3yr) by far more than 30%, but neither is a growth signal: equity shrinks because buybacks + dividends (~RMB9.5bn/yr) exceed earnings, and the 3-year revenue CAGR compounds off the FY2022 lockdown trough (RMB60.7bn). The 4-year revenue CAGR from FY2021 is 4.0%. EPS CAGRs are undefined (negative FY2021/FY2022 base). Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined on the FY2025 endpoint (owner FCF -3,697 after the working-capital unwind); on the TTM-to-June-2026 endpoint (4,438) the series is FY2021 272, FY2022 4,500, FY2023 6,061, FY2024 4,424 -> roughly flat since FY2022.
historical_growth.notes: Only five annual periods (FY2021-FY2025) are available, so the '5yr' figures are 4-year CAGRs (FY2021 -> FY2025). Owner-FCF history strips SBC and net interest income (investment income inside 'Other income' is not in the KPI history before FY2024, so the historical series is on the narrower strip; the TTM base strips both). Reported FCF history (RMB m): FY2021 2,165; FY2022 7,668; FY2023 10,540; FY2024 8,410; FY2025 -984. SBC fell from 3.5-4.1% of revenue (FY2022-23) to 2.0% (FY2025), so the owner-FCF series has been catching up to reported FCF rather than lagging it.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -8.5%: H1 -12.0% reported (existing-home -3.2%, new-home -15.9%, renovation -26.4% on deliberate channel exit, rental -8.5% on the net-fee shift) with Q2 improving to -5.7% and GTV back to +6.3%; H2 assumed -5%. FY2027 +3% as the transaction market stabilises and the rental/renovation revenue optics stop shrinking; FY2028-30 +4% from existing-home share gains (H1 2026 transaction count +18.6% vs a flat market) and rental unit growth (+34% YoY) on a flat-to-slightly-down housing GTV; fade to 2.5% terminal. No formal company guidance exists.
base.margin_rationale: 11.5% FY2026 is below the H1 2026 run-rate (~13.6-14% ex investment income) and above the TTM 9.6%, allowing for H2 seasonality and some reinvestment of the opex cuts; 12.0% thereafter is a mid-cycle level between the FY2025 trough (6.5%) and the FY2023/H1 2026 peaks (~14%). The Carefree Rent net-fee transition and the renovation channel exit raise the margin percentage structurally by shrinking low-margin gross revenue, which is why mid-cycle sits above the simple 7-14% midpoint.
base.tax_rationale: 28% flat: 25% PRC statutory plus withholding tax on repatriation to the Cayman parent (funding buybacks/dividends) and non-deductible SBC. H1 2026 effective rate 28.2%; FY2025's 36% was distorted by impairments and loss-making subsidiaries without deferred tax assets. Cash taxes paid: FY2025 2,347, TTM ~2,000 against modelled year-1 EBIT tax ~2,000. Pillar Two is immaterial (RMB44.7m).
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 0.64% of revenue in FY2025 (608), 1.1% in FY2024 (1,037), 0.56% in H1 2026 (245): asset-light platform. D&A ex-ROU 1.13% FY2025 (934 depreciation + 138 amortisation), 0.9% H1 2026. Paths converge at 0.9% so the terminal year has capex = D&A and no perpetual non-cash tailwind.
base.wc_rationale: 0% capture: working capital is transaction-driven and noisy (developer receivables, commissions payable to agents/stores, renovation contract liabilities, Carefree Rent lease accruals). FY2024 +6.1bn inflow, FY2025 -6.7bn outflow, H1 2026 -2.1bn ex-lease: the swings reverse rather than compound, so no structural capture is credited or charged.

bull.narrative: Policy support (mortgage-rate cuts, purchase-restriction removal, destocking) lifts existing-home volumes from 2027; Beike's share gains compound on a growing pie; the 14% margin seen at the FY2023 peak and the H1 2026 run-rate holds as the structural level because the opex reset and the asset-light rental model are permanent.

bear.narrative: China housing transactions resume their structural decline: new-home GTV keeps contracting as developers deleverage, existing-home volumes roll over after the 2026 bounce, agent and store attrition (agents -3.1%, active agents -7.5%, MAU -6% YoY) erodes ACN liquidity, and the H1 2026 margin proves to be a cost-cut peak that competition and reinvestment pull back toward the FY2024 level (~9%). Revenue falls two more years then crawls at 2%.

scenario_narratives.base: The China housing market is 'smaller but stabilising': FY2026 revenue falls ~8.5% (H1 -12% already reported, Q2 improving, GTV back to growth), then grows 3-4% as Beike takes existing-home share (connected brands now ~68% of GTV, transaction count +18.6% in H1 2026 vs a flat market) and scales the asset-light Carefree Rent book (+34% units). The adjusted EBITDA margin ex investment income settles at 12%, between the FY2025 trough (6.5%) and the FY2023 / H1 2026 peaks (~14%): the opex reset is mostly kept but some is reinvested in AI tooling, agent enablement and service quality. SBC drifts from 2.1% to 1.6% of revenue; capex and D&A converge at 0.9%. Capital returns (~RMB9.5bn/yr of buybacks and dividends) continue out of the RMB63bn treasury, which the model adds to EV at full value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Policy stimulus revives existing-home volumes and the primary market bottoms in 2027; Beike's network effects turn share gains into 6-7% growth on a growing pie, and the 14% margin of H1 2026 holds as the structural level because the cost base was permanently reset and the rental/renovation mix shift is complete. Terminal growth 3% reflects a housing-services platform compounding with Chinese household income.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 bounce is a policy blip: new-home GTV keeps shrinking, existing-home volumes roll over, developer receivables deteriorate, and agent/store attrition weakens the ACN. Margins recede toward the FY2024 level (~9%) as competition for a shrinking GTV pool bids up commission splits and the AI/productivity investments do not pay back. Revenue -12%, -4%, then flat, crawling at 2% from 2030. The VIE structure and PRC regulatory overhang are not modelled as a separate event but are why bear carries 30% weight rather than the 15% house default.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (vs 15% house default): revenue is tied to Chinese housing GTV, which has declined for four years with no proven recovery catalyst; new-home revenue (27% of the mix) depends on stressed developers; the VIE/WVR structure and PRC property/data regulation are single-regulator dependencies that can impair value regardless of operations; and the H1 2026 margin step-up is one half-year old. Bull 20% (vs 35%): the bull case needs policy stimulus, a cyclical volume recovery AND a permanently held 14% margin to all land together. Base 50%. Note that half of the weighted value is net cash, which is the same in every scenario and compresses the spread.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF component DCF on a cyclical, net-cash Chinese housing-services platform. Three choices define the number. (1) Base year: FY2025 owner FCF was negative (RMB-3.7bn) because RMB6.7bn of working capital unwound in a shrinking market, and H1 2026 reversed most of it; neither the FY2025 trough nor the H1 2026 bounce is extrapolated. The forward path is built from components (mid-cycle 12% EBITDA margin, 2% SBC, 0.9% capex) off FY2025 revenue with a -8.5% first year that honours the reported H1 decline, and the disclosed FCF base is the TTM to June 2026. (2) Treasury: RMB64.4bn of cash, deposits, HTM debt and wealth-management products less RMB1.7bn of loans is added to EV at full value, and the RMB1.3bn/yr of interest and investment income it earns is stripped from the flows so the pile is counted once; escrow cash and operating lease liabilities are both excluded. Net cash is ~HK$21.8/share, close to half of the market price, so the operating business is valued at roughly 5-6x owner FCF by the market. (3) Risk: charged once, in the flows and the weights (bear 30%), with a single 10% CNY WACC and a 15x terminal cap for a cyclical; nothing is stacked on the discount rate for property-market or VIE risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: China housing transaction volumes (GTV) resume a structural decline; new-home revenue (27% of mix) and developer receivables are the most exposed
The H1 2026 margin step-up (gross margin +6.7pp, opex -14%) proves to be a one-half-year cost-cut peak rather than a structural 12-14% level
VIE / weighted-voting-rights structure: PRC regulatory action could impair offshore holders' economic rights irrespective of operating performance
Net cash is ~46% of the market price; a repatriation restriction, an onshore-cash haircut, or a large acquisition would remove value the model credits at par
Working-capital swings of RMB6-7bn in either direction make any single year's FCF unrepresentative; the model credits zero structural capture
RMB/HKD rate moves change the HKD value directly; the fx_rate is not refreshed by refresh_price.py
Agent/store/MAU attrition erodes the ACN network effect, the core moat the base case relies on for share gains
